Hi Samir —

Great to be moving this forward. As discussed, attached is a first-pass gating matrix and the workload profile CSV I used to derive concurrency buckets. High-level asks for the MAP benchmarking window:

- Define 3 workload slices (interactive chat, batch-embedding, bulk-inference) with per-slice request distributions attached.
- Measure TTFT (time to first token), median and 95thpct latency per request, and sustained throughput at target concurrencies (see sheet).
- Success criteria (draft): TTFT median <= 120ms, 95thpct <= 350ms for interactive chat; sustained throughput >= 1,000 reqs/min at concurrencies described; no more than 1% token error rate.

Can you confirm these targets are aligned with Helios' acceptance gates? If yes, we'll lock the MAP milestones and target a close timeline that includes procurement the week after benchmarks.

Attachments: gating_matrix_v1.xlsx (workload slices + gating matrix), workload_profiles.csv

Thanks,

Samir / Alex —

Good points, Samir. Quick clarifications on methodology so the gating matrix is repeatable:

- TTFT: we record time from request arrival at API gateway to first generated token emitted by model-serving runtime. We will report median, p95, p99, and cold-start (first request after 15m idle).
- Throughput: sustained throughput measured over 5-minute rolling windows for the target concurrency, plus a 30-minute soak to validate stability.
- Concurrency buckets: we will run at 1x (baseline), 5x, and 10x expected production concurrency; for Helios that maps to [10, 50, 100] concurrent sessions for interactive chat (see workload_profiles.csv).

I pushed a short runbook to the shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/0B-hel-POC-benchmark — it includes the load generator config, metric collectors, and the exact shell steps. I recommend we add a pass/fail gating column per slice: PASS, WARN, FAIL with automated Slack notifications to the MAP channel.

Tessa
Sr. Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: workload gating matrix & TTFT acceptance criteria — Helios POC close plan

Samir —

Thanks — we've updated the gating matrix to include p99 and cold-start rows and added a 30-min spike/soak test. Attached is the MAP timeline (map_timeline_v2.pdf) with proposed milestone dates:

- Week 0 (May 25): benchmark dry-run (internal)
- Week 1 (May 31-Jun 4): formal benchmark window (Helios observers invited)
- Week 2 (Jun 7): results review + acceptance decision
- Week 3 (Jun 14): procurement SOW & final signatures (target)

Success criteria (final draft):
- Interactive chat: TTFT median <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 600ms, cold-start <= 900ms; no more than 1% token error rate across runs.
- Throughput: sustain 1,000 reqs/min with p95 latency <= 400ms at 10x concurrency bucket.
- Stability: no memory growth >5% over 30-minute soak and no server restarts.

Can you confirm acceptance of the timeline and the pass/fail columns so I can lock the MAP and push the invites?

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

All —

Reviewed the updated gating matrix and timeline. Proposed acceptance checkpoints and gating matrix entries (short):

- Pre-benchmark: confirm dataset/seeded prompts and redaction rules.
- Benchmark window: automated run + manual spot-checks; require at least 3 repeat runs per slice to reduce noise.
- Acceptance decision: PASS if all slices PASS; WARN if any WARN and remediation plan accepted; FAIL if any FAIL and no remediation accepted.

Milestone commitments: let’s aim for a decision call on Jun 7 at 10am PT. If PASS, we will fast-track procurement and target signature by Jun 14. I updated the HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345-HEL-4387 — added milestone checklist and assigned owners.
